Hi André,

I just tried setting my credentials in this manner using a fresh installation of `mcera5` (the package that `micro_era5` relies upon and that I maintain) on a cloud RStudio session and it worked fine on my end. The uid and cds_api_key are not the same as the log in username/password, but are listed on the CDS website: once you have logged in, click on your name in the upper right, and scroll down to "API Key". They should be listed there.

Your uid should be 5 digits, and your CDS API key should be the following #'s of digits (separated by dashes): 8 - 4 - 4 - 4 - 12

If this is what you have been using and it still does not work, could you provide me your session info via `devtools::session_info()`, in particular the version of `ecmwfr` you are using?

Best,
Dave

messages.author: 2bcecdd9c0443e65
messages.subject: Re: era5 download issues
parts:
Hi André,

If by model you mean the NicheMapR microclimate model, yes most of the NicheMapR wrapper functions that leverage the microclimate model have some option to save downloaded climate and re-access the local data, or you can modify one of the wrapper functions to access a custom climate dataset (from experience this may take a bit of effort). However I want to note that for all of the NicheMapR wrapper functions– including micro_era5 that uses mcera5– once you download the climate dataset once, if you set save = 1 then the climate forcing data will be saved (setting save = 2 will access saved climate data). For downloading ERA5 data via mcera5, I want to note that the download times are mostly due to the CDS API server, which is out of control of mcera5 and will be the case no matter what fashion you download CDS data. But, once downloaded, you won't need to do so again for the same time and place.

Best,
Dave
ᐧ

messages.subject: Re: era5 download issues
parts:
Hi Liang,

Sorry I missed your latest response. Yes, although I haven't experimented much with areas as large as you have requested here (ie -90 to 90 latitude), I imagine this will exceed quotas that the Climate Data Store allows for a single request. Furthermore mcera5 isn't designed to download such large swathes of the planet at once. You'd be better off iterating through smaller areas, to start!

Best,
Dave

On Wednesday, November 9, 2022 at 10:44:57 AM UTC+8 dkli...@gmail.com wrote:
Hi André,

If by model you mean the NicheMapR microclimate model, yes most of the NicheMapR wrapper functions that leverage the microclimate model have some option to save downloaded climate and re-access the local data, or you can modify one of the wrapper functions to access a custom climate dataset (from experience this may take a bit of effort). However I want to note that for all of the NicheMapR wrapper functions– including micro_era5 that uses mcera5– once you download the climate dataset once, if you set save = 1 then the climate forcing data will be saved (setting save = 2 will access saved climate data). For downloading ERA5 data via mcera5, I want to note that the download times are mostly due to the CDS API server, which is out of control of mcera5 and will be the case no matter what fashion you download CDS data. But, once downloaded, you won't need to do so again for the same time and place.

Best,
Dave

The uid and cds_api_key are not the same as the log in username/password, but are listed on the CDS website: once you have logged in, click on your name in the upper right, and scroll down to "API Key". Your uid should be 5 digits, and your CDS API key should be the following #'s of digits (separated by dashes): 8 - 4 - 4 - 4 - 12

If this is what you have been using and it still does not work, could you provide me your session info via `devtools::session_info()`, in particular the version of `ecmwfr` you are using?
